questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Going to Asia. Singapore is a perfect place to explore the surrounding countries as the flights are cheap and you can travel a lot.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite chaotic arriving in Singapore. There are a lot of formalities that you need to do within the first couple of weeks and everybody was stressing out about it. Be sure to check all the e-mails NUS send you, book appointments dates as soon as possible and be sure to show up :D

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not a lot. Only e-mails. There were different whatsapp groups with other exchange students that was helpful!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You can apply for housing trough NUS. They do not have room for all applicants so you might be unlucky. I got answer for my application about one month before leaving for Singapore, which was a bit late and left me a bit frustrated.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I stayed at an RC - Tembusu College - which had a meal plan that you had to pay for to stay there. Breakfast and dinner six days a week. Food was alright - four different stalls to choose from.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Fun and good way to get to know other people! Try to get a room with AC lol

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Got answers for my modules a couple days before starting classes which was chaotic:)

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I can't haha. Very confusing and time consuming - they send you mails with reminders and guides of what to do though so just follow them

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had no problems but met others who did not get the classes that they has chosen in their application.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just be sure to apply for modules that are available for exchange students. When you apply for modules you can chose modules that you are not allowed for and won't get so you have to find the list of modules for exchange students on NUS website.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was not able to get any modules relating to my major. The classes was alright - mostly big lectures. A lot of AC in the rooms so remember warm clothes even though its 35 degrees outside.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: You can apply for 1, 2 and 3 year courses. I had some first year courses and all the people I was studying was quite young. If you want "easy" classes to pass and more time to travel and enjoy Singapore/Asia apply for "introduction" classes!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More focused on lectures and MCQ tests.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Plants and Society, Introduction to Psychology, Enviromental Politics and Ecology and environment

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Enviromental Politics was fun and engaging. Would not recommend the other courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Food is very cheap and good! A lot of foodstalls around campus for lunch and dinner:)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Nightlife is EXPENSIVE

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: NUS is big on social activities and sports - all students participate in something!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Whatever you feel like:) I played a lot of football and climbing!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Phillipines, South Korea, Indonesia!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: People are very nice - talk with them:) A lot of whatsapp groups with events and socialising.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really anything.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: HAWKER CENTERS!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Its very hot. You can travel all of Asia cheap and convenient!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Travelling.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Can be lonely at times:) Make sure to call home!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
